messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I have a task to do, it need to pull the test from a file and do check on those words and count number of words( it is almost similar to word count. A few conditions added on them)

For this I wrote two different programs, both are working fine and giving the same result. Not sure which one is correct in terms of efficiency and load

Here is the first one: written an input format function to do the task

ur <- url('http://jmlr.org/papers/volume5/lewis04a/a11-smart-stop-list/english.stop',open="r") # Connection to a url has stopwords

stopwords <- readLines(ur) # reading stop words

close(ur) #Closing url connection

# Input format function to clean the text and get the desired output

input.format.custom <- function(con,nrecs)

{

  lines <- readLines(con,1)

  if (length(lines) == 0)

    NULL

  else {

    strings <- tolower(unlist(strsplit(lines, split="\\s+"))) # List of words in lower case

    ptrn <- '^http.*?'; ndx = grep(ptrn, strings, perl=T); strings[-ndx] # Identifying words starting with http and removing those words

    strings <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", strings) # Removing special characters

    StopwordMatch <- match(strings,c(stopwords,"","*")) #Customizing stopwords and matching with strings

    strings <- strings[is.na <http://is.na>(StopwordMatch)] #Removing stopwords

    tOfwords <- tapply(strings,strings,length)

    Word.Count <- data.frame(Words=names(tOfwords),counts=unname(tOfwords))

    keyval(NULL,Word.Count)

  }

}

input.format.read = make.input.format(format = input.format.custom, mode = "text")

rmr.options(backend="hadoop")

d <- from.dfs(mapreduce(input='/hdfs/hdfp/NEWS',input.format=input.format.read,map=function(k,v) keyval(k,v)))

Here is the second one: written an map reduce function to do the task

ur <- url('http://jmlr.org/papers/volume5/lewis04a/a11-smart-stop-list/english.stop',open="r") # Connection to a url has stopwords

stopwords <- readLines(ur) # reading stop words

close(ur) #Closing url connection

# map  function to clean the text and get the desired output

tm.map <- function(con,nrecs)

{

    strings <- tolower(unlist(strsplit(nrecs, split="\\s+"))) # List of words in lower case

    ptrn <- '^http.*?'; ndx = grep(ptrn, strings, perl=T); strings[-ndx] # Identifying words starting with http and removing those words

    strings <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", strings) # Removing special characters

    StopwordMatch <- match(strings,c(stopwords,"","*")) #Customizing stopwords and matching with strings

    strings <- strings[is.na <http://is.na>(StopwordMatch)] #Removing stopwords

    tOfwords <- tapply(strings,strings,length)

    Word.Count <- data.frame(Words=names(tOfwords),counts=unname(tOfwords))

    keyval(NULL,Word.Count)

}

rmr.options(backend="hadoop")

d <- from.dfs(mapreduce(input='/hdfs/hdfp/NEWS',input.format="text",map=tm.map))

Here are my question:

1.       Which program is efficient?

2.       If I use input format function to do the task, where the execution of cleaning is (is it in Hadoop or local)

Other points: you can ask me why I have done count of words map task and generate it value and key as null. The answer I observed was, input put file has ~50k words after splitting and when I pass all those words as keys my program returning an error message saying maximum limit of map task reached. So I kept it in a table and passed it as values.

One more observation:

I had used rmr.options to reset the # of map tasks as (rmr.options(backend="hadoop",backend.parameters=list(hadoop=list('D=mapred.reduce.tasks=10','D=mapred.map.tasks=100','D=mapred.tasktracker.map.tasks.maximum=1000'))) but this seems no effect on the process. I check the logs in ‘/logs/userlogs/job_201402011706_0047/’ directory I could see a job-acls.xml(this file exists in each job’s directory) file and it has some options set for the job. I feel this file should include those parameters what we set in the rmr.options statement, but not set in the file.

Please help me.

Regards,

Sivaji

help(package="rmr2")

to.dfs(from.dfs(.... as before, works))

Another possibility, and the reason I've been a little incommunicado, is that rmr2 3.0.0 is available as of today. I should be more efficient particularly when working with data frames and many distinct keys.

Antonio

Antonio,

Great work on rmr2 3.0.0!

It looks like some of the responses on the SO comment indicate a possible memory leak.

I'm curious if you ever found any resolution to this issue, and if any of it possibly made it into 3.0.0?  (I'm currently running into the same issue...)

Drew

> >
> > The short answer is to set upper limit of head size for map/reduce tasks. After I set 700 MB heap size, my task uses only 300MB physical memory, but 4.2 GB virtual memory. I guess with heap boundary, each container load fewer replica to make sure that it won't exceed the limit. It seems to me that, in YARN it's still user's responsibility to do memory control, making sure there's enough space to run R.
> >
> > Thanks for you response. Hope rmr2 become more compatible sooner.
> >
> > -Lishu
> >
> >
> > On Thursday, January 9, 2014 11:46:18 AM UTC-6, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:
> > > Hi,
> > > first I have to admit I don't know the answer right away and I will investigate further. rmr2 doesn't directly access YARN and doesn't know anything about containers. rmr2 is using hadoop streaming which uses mapreduce which uses YARN. So you may be able to gather more information by searching for streaming and YARN and similar queries. Without more detail about your program is hard to guess why it would take more memory with more replication. If each replica is associated with a different key, the reducer need only load the data for one key at a time, unless there is a bug of course. One thing that I don't know and that could be of interest is whether the R process is included in the container. With streaming there are two processes for each task attempt: a java process and an R process. With mr1, from a memory management point of view, hadoop mapreduce ignored the R process. One had to make sure that the number of slots was small enough and the amount of memory allocated to the jvm small enough to leave room for R. With containers, this situation may have changed. There were some streaming bugs that prevented us from switching to mr2 for quite some time, so testing was impossible both internally and for our users. messages.body_plain:
rmr2 doesn't know anything about classes. It relies on hadoop streaming working properly (which is a java program and needs access to the necessary libraries -- the piece that is failing in your case).

A test program, adapted from the streaming tutorial, is

```
$HADOOP_CMD  jar $HADOOP_STREAMING/hadoop-streaming.jar \
    -input /path/to/text/file \
    -output /path/to/out/dir \
    -mapper /bin/cat \
    -reducer /bin/wc
```

Set the variables, replace the input and output with real hdfs files, and this should work. If it doesn't, you don't have hadoop correctly installed and you need to refer to the instructions of whatever distribution you have. If it does, it's more likely an rmr2 problem, albeit this is unlikely from the type of error. I hope this helps

Antonio
